lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 3: Full Cycle of a Deep Learning Project

unit.name: Data quality, distribution mismatch, and model capacity
unit.description: Explains why data quality matters, why training data need not perfectly match the test distribution, and how large model capacity changes the tradeoff.
unit.summary: Data quality matters because low-quality examples, such as blurry face images, can be less useful than sharp in-focus examples when they do not match the desired recognition setting [ts=1925s]. The instructor then addresses distribution mismatch: training data should be relevant, but it does not always need to come from exactly the same distribution as the test set [ts=1981s]. Larger neural networks can often absorb somewhat irrelevant but non-incorrect data without hurting the core task as much as smaller models would [ts=2034s]. This section bridges data choices to deployment by returning to the trained face-recognition model as software that must run inference in a real system [ts=2211s].

key_points.text: Data quality matters; for face recognition, sharp in-focus images are generally higher quality than blurry images.
Training data should be close to the target task, but exact train-test distribution matching is less absolute with modern large neural networks.
Large neural networks can often use somewhat irrelevant but non-incorrect data without much degradation on the core task.
Incorrect data is still harmful even if irrelevant data may hurt less for high-capacity neural networks.
A trained model becomes a deployed software component that accepts inputs and returns a recognition decision.

kp_catalog.description: Data quality and distribution similarity matter, but modern large neural networks can often tolerate some relevant or slightly irrelevant non-incorrect data.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The section provides practical guidance on blur, high-quality text, distribution similarity, large networks, and the continued danger of incorrect data [ts=1925s] [ts=2034s].

kp_catalog.name: Deployment as model-serving software
kp_catalog.description: A trained model becomes a software service or local component that accepts inputs, runs inference, and returns product decisions under cost and latency constraints.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Deployment constraints motivate VAD, edge/cloud choices, and monitoring; the lecture explicitly distinguishes a trained model from a deployed product [ts=2211s] [ts=2247s].
